solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bath love seat could provide privileged position

indicators.note: the letters of the three words could be rearranged to provide something new, so they are shuffled

explanation.surface: A loving couple's bench in the city of Bath might give someone a favoured spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could provide' rearranges BATH LOVE SEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: at old dining tables the salt cellar divided honoured guests from lesser ones, so sitting beyond it on the near side marked high status.

clue.text: Alto and bass head on to North Central region

parts.note: A is the musical abbreviation for alto
B is the musical abbreviation for bass
dome is slang for the head

explanation.surface: Choir parts being steered towards some northern area of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on to' simply strings the pieces together in order.
explanation.definitionFit: The belly is the middle section of the body, between chest and pelvis.

clue.text: Book contains nothing evil — short shock turns up at the end

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing
bad means evil

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters are read from bottom to top
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a shock of hair is a thick mass of it

explanation.surface: A volume holds nothing wicked, though a jolt arrives at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' is hair, not a fright; 'short' docks its last letter and 'turns up' reverses the rest, read upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Obadiah is the shortest book of the Old Testament, named after its prophet.

clue.text: Active criminal Green's name going round

indicators.note: criminal suggests wrongdoing, so these letters are bent out of their order
going round means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: to cite is to name, as in naming a source

explanation.surface: A lively offender called Green whose name keeps doing the rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges the colour word; 'name' is the verb to cite, which 'going round' turns back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone full of vigour and energy is active.

clue.text: Measure of poet's pigeon

definitions.meaning: a Hebrew unit of capacity, about ten bushels
the Greek epic poet of the Iliad, with 's as a link
a homing pigeon, trained to fly back to its loft

explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: three senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names an ancient Hebrew measure, the blind Greek poet and a racing pigeon.

clue.text: Socially acceptable bishop in impression that's bizarre

indicators.note: in means these pieces sit inside the impression word

parts.note: a seal is an impression stamped in wax
U means upper-class and so socially acceptable, from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U
RR, Right Reverend, is a bishop's title

explanation.surface: A proper churchman leaves a strange mark on people.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old label for upper-class usage; 'in' places URR inside SEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something dreamlike and strange is bizarre.

clue.text: Surgery school?

definitions.meaning: piercing a boil with a blade is minor surgery
a public school in West Sussex, England

explanation.walkthrough: Lancing College is a well-known English independent boarding school near Brighton.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting open an abscess is a surgical act, and the same word names an English school.

clue.text: Politically pink, perhaps, that could stand as Conservative?

definitions.meaning: C, the abbreviation for Conservative, is the leftmost letter of the word centre

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is cryptic: the C standing for Conservative sits on the left of the word CENTRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a moderate leftist politician sits slightly towards the socialist side of the spectrum.

clue.text: Play moves before mating

definitions.meaning: the final phase of a chess game, before checkmate

explanation.walkthrough: 'mating' is the checkmate of chess, not romance.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the title of a Beckett drama and the last stage of a chess game.

clue.text: Sailor having broken arm in A&E in Boston

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: ER, the emergency room, is the American name for A&E

explanation.surface: A seaman with a fractured limb in hospital casualty in Massachusetts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges ARM to MAR. A&E is the British casualty department; Americans say ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a seaman, as in Coleridge's Ancient Mariner.

clue.text: Third hangman executed personal assistant

indicators.note: executed means carried out or put to death, signalling the words are made over in a new form

explanation.surface: A third executioner put to death, a grim joke at the gallows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executed' rearranges THIRD HANGMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a trusted chief helper or aide is someone's closest assistant.

clue.text: Unwarranted interference with no hesitation in filling a hole

indicators.note: with no says the hesitation sound is dropped from the longer word

parts.note: tampering is meddling without right
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Meddling without pausing while plugging a gap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes ER from TAMPERING.
explanation.definitionFit: Packing down earth or a charge into a hole is the act of ramming it in firmly.

clue.text: Dancing bird in front of fish

indicators.note: in front of says the bird comes before the fish

parts.note: a ree, or reeve, is the female ruff
the ling is a long fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A bird doing a jig ahead of a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: REE, the female ruff, is a crossword stalwart.
explanation.definitionFit: Dancing a Scottish reel, or whirling about, is described by this participle.

clue.text: Loud creep gets bird

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical direction for loud
to inch is to creep slowly

explanation.surface: A noisy sneak ends up with a feathered pet.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small seed-eating songbird such as the goldfinch.

clue.text: Steps to attic of the highest class

definitions.meaning: the uppermost staircase in a house, leading to the loft

explanation.walkthrough: A double definition: a literal staircase and a figurative rank.
explanation.definitionFit: The uppermost set of stairs, and by extension the best division or rank.

clue.text: Teacher of sports class died overseeing game in fever

parts.note: PE is physical education

indicators.note: in says the game sits inside the fever word

parts.note: ague is a malarial fever
go is the Japanese board game

explanation.surface: A gym teacher died while supervising a match during an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overseeing' works in a down clue: PED sits above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym, often a pedantic one: a schoolmaster or instructor.

clue.text: Safely established wall bracket finally?

definitions.meaning: a sconce is a wall bracket for candles; something finally put in a sconce is whimsically ...

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading treats the verb as 'put in a sconce', a sconce being a candle bracket on a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone comfortably and securely settled somewhere is snugly installed there.

clue.text: Shut off obscene broadcast after little time

indicators.note: after says the sound comes after the short time

parts.note: sec is short for second, a little time

indicators.note: broadcast means the word is heard, not read

parts.note: lewd means obscene

explanation.surface: Censors blocking a smutty transmission after a brief delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' signals a sound-alike of the word for obscene; 'after' puts it behind the brief time.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to isolate or keep apart from others.

clue.text: Very forward pupil beginning to yield to Oscar

parts.note: on means forward, as in 'move on'
L is a learner, as on L-plates

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter is taken

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A cheeky student starts to give in to the Academy Award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' takes Y from 'yield'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: as in 'only too happy', meaning extremely or very.

clue.text: Article leads to thank you letter

parts.note: the definite article comes first, leading the way to the thanks
ta is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece prompts a grateful note.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is a casual British 'thanks'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the eighth character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Novice's support in wet weather? On the contrary

indicators.note: in signals one piece inside another
on the contrary flips the stated order, so the weather goes into the support

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball
rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: A beginner's prop for a rainy day, or is it the reverse?
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the support goes in the wet weather; 'On the contrary' turns that round, so the weather goes inside the golf peg instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone being trained is a beginner or learner.

clue.text: Smooth happening around corresponding university

indicators.note: around says the happening word encloses the other piece

parts.note: an event is a happening
the OU, Open University, teaches by correspondence

explanation.surface: A smooth occasion with a university that writes back.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open University is Britain's distance-learning university, once taught by post.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb: to level off or make uniform, removing bumps.

clue.text: Soft touches? No credit, not one shilling!

parts.note: tick is credit, as in buying on tick

indicators.note: not one says a single letter is dropped from the longer word

parts.note: no means without, so -less
s is the abbreviation for the old shilling

explanation.surface: Gentle caresses on offer? Not on credit, not for a single coin!
explanation.walkthrough: No credit is TICK-LESS; 'not one' drops one S. A shilling was a pre-1971 British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural noun: light, gentle strokes that may make someone laugh.

clue.text: Support parade

definitions.meaning: a brace or bar that holds a structure up
to walk showily, as a verb

explanation.walkthrough: A double definition: a structural brace and a swaggering walk.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a bracing beam and a vain swagger.

clue.text: Indian state leader is 3

definitions.note: points to the answer of 3-down, a synonym for active, so 'is 3' means 'is lively'

parts.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast
a head is a leader

explanation.surface: A chief minister of an Indian state counts as the third.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' refers to the answer of 3-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone enterprising and vigorous is lively and full of drive.

clue.text: Almost identical to king's circumference

indicators.note: almost says the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: equal means identical
R is rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A circle nearly the same as a monarch's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts EQUAL to EQUA.
explanation.definitionFit: The imaginary line running round the Earth's widest point is its girth.

clue.text: Shop unit and logo revamped

indicators.note: revamped means remodelled, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A store fitting and brand emblem given a makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revamped' rearranges AND LOGO.
explanation.definitionFit: In retail, a freestanding island of shelving is called by the name of a Venetian boat.

clue.text: Illegal position of trousers

definitions.meaning: unfair, from a foul blow in boxing
trousers are worn beneath the waist belt

explanation.walkthrough: In boxing, hitting under the waistband is a foul.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom from boxing: a blow under the waist is against the rules, hence unfair.
